body:
Reported by the user (filed by an agent): on main after v0.15.0 (`d251029`), three snapshot tests fail with 23 differing pixels each:

- `egui_app::tests::egui_shell_snapshot`
- `egui_app::tests::egui_shell_snapshot_light`
- `egui_app::tests::tool_editor_snapshot`

- The three snapshots pass on main.
- A test pins that the toolbar label doesn't change with `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`: it renders the fixed test version.

title: Viewport: orthographic (parallel) projection option
body:
## What are you trying to do

I machine plates and brackets on my LinuxCNC machine, and most of my viewport time is setup work: looking straight at a side to line something up, judging an edge for parallelism, checking the part against the world axes, and reading the toolpath overlays. The view cube gives me the orientation (top/front/side is one click), but the projection stays perspective: edges converge, the silhouette drifts while I orbit or zoom, and a side view never looks "straight" the way a machinist's square looks straight. For CAM layout work I want a parallel (orthographic) projection most of the time.

This is the normal CAD/CAM convention - Fusion 360 defaults to a parallel projection with a perspective toggle next to it, and OnShape and SolidWorks do the same.

## How you imagine it working

- A Perspective / Orthographic radio pair beside the Shaded/Wireframe radios in the viewport panel. Default stays Perspective, so the current look never changes on open.
- A keyboard shortcut for the flip, in the same layer as the existing F/V/... keys.
- In ortho mode, the wheel scales the view height instead of the orbit distance; zoom-to-cursor stays cursor-anchored; and picking and every overlay (toolpaths, boundary viz, the view-cube HUD) read the same matrix the draw does, so nothing drifts.
- The view-cube face views become true ortho views in that mode. The mode rides as view state - a direct field flip like the display mode, never a command, never saved into the project.

Happy to build this - claim comment to follow.

title: Post gate refuses a clean 2D Contour: the column sim's inscribed arc chords clip a convex corner and read it as a 10 mm gouge

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
A 2D Contour around a plain L-shaped block generates with only the expected "Top below stock" rapid warning, but the post gate refuses it for a **10 mm gouge that isn't there**. The column engine of the program sim cuts each XY arc as chords drawn *inside* the arc (`arc_chords` at `chord_tol = cell / 4` = 0.094 mm). On a convex corner, the arc's centre is the part's own corner, so the simulated tool centre moves up to one sagitta closer to the part than the real G2/G3 does. One 0.375 mm column whose centre is 0.088 mm inside the corner gets clipped. Because the verdict judges each column by height alone, that clip counts as a gouge the full height of the wall.

Nothing unsafe reaches G-code: the gate *refuses* the post. But a correct program can't be posted, so this is a P1, not a P0.

### Part (our own geometry; rebuild it in any CAD)
In XZ, the profile is (-40,0) (40,0) (40,15) (10,15) (10,25) (-40,25), extruded from y -30 to 30. That gives a riser 25 mm high over x -40..10 and a lower step at z 15 over x 10..40. Export it as STEP.

### Reproduce (upstream/main 13802a1, `camcraft-cli mcp`)
1. `import_model {path: <part>.step, name: "StepBlock"}`
2. `set_stock {box: {dx: 90, dy: 70, dz: 28}}`, which puts the stock at x -45..45, y -35..35, z 0..28
3. `add_tool {catalog: "EM-0600-4FL"}`
4. `add_operation {kind: "2D Contour", tool: "EM-0600-4FL", name: "Contour1", source: "StepBlock"}` with default params: climb, side auto, stepdown 5, leave 0, top = top of model, bottom = bottom of model
5. `generate`, then `verify`

`verify` output:
- `rapid_in_stock`: "rapid move 1 travels below the clearance plane inside stock". This one is legitimate: top of model 25 is below stock top 28 and nothing faced it. It goes away with a Face op first, and the gouge stays.
- `post_gate`: **"gouge: program cuts below the model in 1 cell(s), worst 10.00 mm at (9.94, -29.94, z 15.00)"**

The same gouge shows with a Face op at stock top -3 ahead of the contour.

### Which moves
The contour walks the riser's section (x -40..10, offset by r = 3) at z 25, 20 and 15. Lower levels are skipped ("the part is solid below it"). Each level starts with the same corner arc around the riser's convex corner (10, -30):

```
  3 Feed (2.399,-33.902,25)->(10.346,-32.980,25)
  4 Feed (10.346,-32.980,25)->(13.000,-30.000,25) arc centre (10,-30)  <- R = 3 exactly
 19 / 34: the same arc at z 20 / z 15
```

Replaying the moves one at a time on the same `Dexel` (cell 0.375, x0 -45, y0 -35) lowers column (146,13), centre (9.9375, -29.9375), at **moves 4, 19 and 34 only**: 28 -> 25 -> 20 -> 15. The part's top at that centre is 25, which gives the 10 mm reading.

### Diagnosis: a verifier false positive from arc chord sagitta
- **The real path never touches that point.** The column centre is 0.088 mm from the corner, diagonally into the riser. The exact arc keeps the tool centre 3.000 mm from the corner, on the opposite side, so the nearest tool centre is about 3.06 mm away from the column centre. The cutter edge stays clear of it by about 0.06 mm. The generator-time verify finds no gouge.
- **The simulated path does touch it.** `Dexel::subtract` (crates/sim/src/stock_sim/dexel.rs) splits an XY arc with `cl::arc_chords(.., chord_tol)` and `chord_tol = dex.cell * 0.25` (cut.rs `simulate`). For this arc the first chord, (10.3457,-32.9800)->(11.6954,-32.4750), has a sagitta of about 0.086 mm, so its midpoint is 2.914 mm from the corner. Its distance to the column centre is **2.994 mm < r**. `cut_chord`'s exact reach test then lowers the column to z 25/20/15.
- **The height-only verdict blows it up.** `deviate` charges `sim - part` = 15 - 25 = -10, the full riser above the step. So a 6 µm overlap made up by the discretisation reads as a 10 mm gouge.
- Whether a column centre lands inside the sagitta band next to a convex corner depends on the lattice phase. That's why only this one corner of the four convex corners convicts.
- A related but separate effect: #299, a column a few µm inside a straight wall, judged by height alone. Fix 1 there (lateral slack in the verdict) would hide this case only if the slack is at least the chord sagitta. The cause here is in the sweep itself and is fixable on its own.

### Suggested fix (owner's call)
Make the column engine's swept disc never stand closer to the arc centre than the true arc does:
- Option A: cut XY arcs with an exact arc reach (distance from the column centre to the arc, the way `reach` is exact for segments).
- Option B: use circumscribed chords instead of inscribed ones (vertices pushed out by the sagitta) for the material-removal sweep.

Either way, a chord error must never push the simulated tool into the part. Check the bull/ball/cone kernels (`subtract_bull`, `subtract_ball`, `subtract_cone`) for the same issue.

**Done means:** this job (or a synthetic L-block in a box stock whose lattice puts a column centre within one sagitta of a convex corner) verifies with no gouge and posts. A test pins it. The existing gouge goldens still convict real gouges, including a deliberately undersized contour offset at a convex corner.

title: Flip (mirror) an axis, not just turn: e.g. X pointing left with Y to the back and Z up

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Requested by the maintainer (2026-11-08):

> In all of the manipulation we can do to the world/coordinate axes, we have turn x, y, z plus and minus.. but we don't have the "flip axis".. in some cases we need X pointing left and Z up.. but that makes Y point the wrong way and it needs to be "inverted".. I need X to point left and Y towards the back.. and I cannot achieve that by just turning the axes, it needs to be flipped / mirrored.

## Why turning can't do it
X left, Y back, Z up is the basis (-X, +Y, +Z): determinant -1, a **left-handed** frame. Every rotation (turn about X/Y/Z, the presets of #326/#341, the plane picks of #330) keeps handedness, so no combination of turns reaches it - only a reflection (mirror one axis) does. The part-alignment and work-offset code deliberately accepts rigid transforms only (#341 refuses a non-rigid transform in a file as corrupt), so this is a new capability, not a missing preset.

## Why this is safety-critical
Machine coordinate systems are right-handed by standard (ISO 841 / RS-274). A mirrored frame changes the meaning of the program: arc direction (G2 <-> G3), cutter-compensation side (G41 <-> G42), climb vs conventional milling, thread hand, and canned cycles that assume a direction. Getting this wrong cuts a mirror-image part or gouges. Any mirror support must be explicit, labelled, and either compensated consistently through generation, verification and post, or refused by name.

## Open questions (why needs-research)
Which of these is actually wanted - they are different features:
1. **View / display only** - see the part and axes as if standing at the back of the machine (axes triad and viewport flipped), with no change to geometry or the posted program. Lowest risk.
2. **Machine axis direction** - the machine's X+ physically moves the other way (or the operator stands at the back); a per-machine `.mch` setting whose post writes the axis with inverted sign, while the CAM side stays right-handed. Needs a per-post check for G2/G3, G41/G42 and arc-centre sign handling.
3. **Mirror the part** - machine the opposite-hand part (left/right versions of one design): reflect the geometry and regenerate, so toolpaths, arcs and comp sides are correct for the mirrored part (not a mirrored program).
4. **Controller mirror image** (G51.1 / mirror-image function): post a mirror command and let the control mirror - only where the dialect supports it, refused elsewhere.
Also decide: per setup (like #326 alignment) or per document; how it shows in the WCS (#342) and setup sheet; interaction with rotated-offset refusal (#315) and the axis-fit/rotary code.

## Proposed breakdown (after the questions are answered)
- [ ] Decide which of 1-4 (one or more) and record it
- [ ] Display flip (if wanted)
- [ ] Machine axis-direction setting + post sign handling + G2/G3/G41/G42 tests (if wanted)
- [ ] Part mirror as a new geometry operation with handedness-aware regeneration (if wanted)
- [ ] Refusals by name everywhere the mirror is not supported

Related: #326 (PR #341 part alignment), #330 (plane picks), #342 (one WCS per setup), #315 (rotated offsets refused), #308.

title: Face and edge alignment trust facet winding - an inverted mesh lays the part upside down silently

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
From the independent re-review of PR #346 (#330), also true for the single-face pick and the 3-2-1 work-offset alignment (#187).

Face outward normals for alignment picks come from the facets' winding (`outward_normal`, used by `crates/app/src/pick/plane.rs` and `pick/align.rs`). **Done means:** at import (or on first use), each closed body's winding is checked against its signed volume; an inside-out body is either repaired (all facets flipped, with a load note naming the body) or refused by name for alignment picks ("Face 12 belongs to a body whose facets are inside-out ..."); an open/non-manifold body whose outside can't be determined refuses face-normal picks by name. title: Browser tree: each setup owns its WCS, Stock, Machine, Post, Fixtures and Tool list

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Requested by the maintainer (2026-11-08): "The 'Machine', 'Post' should have their own sections in the browser tree under its selected setup. Instead of living under 'stock', 'Fixture' and 'Tool list' should live in the browser under respective setup as well.. As they are setup specific, and editable."

## Today (main)
- `SetupDef` stores `stock`, `wcs`, `datum_from`, `work_offset` - **no machine and no post**: both are document-wide.
- Fixtures already bind to a setup (`FixtureDef.setup`), but the browser shows them under Stock.
- Tools are a document-wide list in a top-level **Tools** browser section; the per-setup tool list exists only as a derived view (setup sheet / Setups page).
- Machine and Post are reached from the ribbon, not the tree.

## What it should be
Each setup in the browser is a node with its own editable children, in this order:

```
Setup1
  WCS            (one per setup - #342; label G54..G59 set on the setup)
  Stock
  Machine        (the setup's machine file)
  Post           (the setup's post processor + its options)
  Fixtures       (the setup's workholding, each fixture a child)
  Tool list      (the tools this setup's operations use, editable)
  Operations     (1+n ops, in machining order)
Setup2
  ...
```

Clicking a node opens its editor (the existing Stock / Machine / Post / Tools pages scoped to that setup); every edit stays an undoable command.

## Per-node behaviour (maintainer, 2026-11-08 - issue comment)
- **Setup selection:** the active setup is chosen with a **radio button** on each setup node in the browser tree (one active at a time; `ActivateSetup`, undoable).
- **Clicking a setup** opens its settings in the right pane, including the **stock source**: use its own stock, or inherit the machined stock from the previous setup in the tree (#317/#320). The first setup has no inherit option.
- **WCS:** opens a right-pane dialog for setting the setup's WCS (origin, 3-2-1 / numeric) and its name, the post label **G54-G59** (#342: one WCS per setup; the label is what the post writes).
- **Stock:** as it is today.
- **Machine:** opens the machine selector in the right pane (for now).
- **Post:** opens the post selector in the right pane (for now).
- **Fixtures:** loading and positioning fixtures for this setup.
- **Tool list:** opens a right-pane dialog with a table of the tools added to this setup and the tool-list export.
- **Operations:** as now - a 1+n tree of the setup's operations; clicking one opens its dialog in the right pane.

## Model changes this needs
- **Machine and Post per setup:** add them to the setup (default: the document's current machine/post, so existing files load and post byte-identically). Two setups may use different machines/posts (e.g. a mill then a lathe). Posting a program that spans setups with different posts writes one file per post (or refuses by name - decide and record).
- **Tool list per setup:** decide between (a) a per-setup tool library (tools copied/assigned per setup) and (b) the document library with a per-setup filtered, editable view (editing a tool edits it everywhere it is used - must say so). Record the decision; keep tool numbers unique per setup's program.
- **Fixtures:** move from under Stock to the setup's own Fixtures node (no model change - `FixtureDef.setup` already exists).
- Project file version bump; old files: every setup takes the document's machine/post; fixtures keep their binding.

## Done means
The tree shows the per-setup structure above; each node opens its scoped editor; machine and post are stored per setup with the migration above; fixtures and tool list appear under their setup; undo/redo for every edit; posting stays byte-identical for single-setup documents; UI tests for the tree structure and node actions; shell snapshots regenerated.

Related: #342 (one WCS per setup), #45 (setup navigation / op ordering in the browser), #148 and #287 (machine editor / machines pane), #322 (Setups reachable), #308 (multi-setup chain).

title: Align the model by picking a face or two edges onto a G17/G18/G19 plane

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Requested by the maintainer (2026-11-08), part of the setup/orientation problem: "a Face or two edges should be possible to locate to a G17-G19 plane as a shortcut to the turn and tilt offset functions - this is on the model."

## What
A one-click way to orient the **model** (not the work offset) by picking geometry:

- **Pick a planar face** -> choose a target plane: **G17 (XY)**, **G18 (ZX)** or **G19 (YZ)**. The model is rotated so that face lies on/parallel to the chosen plane, its outward normal along the plane's axis (+Z for G17, +Y for G18, +X for G19; a "flip" toggle for the opposite direction).
- **Pick two edges** (two non-parallel linear edges, or two coplanar edges) -> they define a plane the same way, and the first edge also fixes the rotation about the plane normal (it is laid along the plane's first axis: X for G17/G18, Y for G19).
- Optionally, place the result: snap the picked face onto the plane's level (e.g. face to Z=0) or keep the model's current position.

It is a shortcut for the existing turn/tilt (rotate model) functions: the same rotation, computed from the pick instead of typed angles.

## Where it fits
- It acts on the **model orientation** - the part's alignment. With #326 (per-setup part alignment to the setup's frame) it should write that setup's part alignment (so a second setup can lay a different face down); until #326 lands, it uses the document-level model transform (`MoveModel`).
- It does **not** rotate the work offset (that path is #187's 3-2-1, now refused when rotated by #315/PR #325) - program zero stays a plain translation (#196 / PR #328).

## Rules
- One undoable command (the same command the rotate/tilt functions use, with the computed rotation), written on command creation.
- Refuse by name: a non-planar face; two parallel or coincident edges, or a curved edge; a degenerate face; a pick on something that is not the model.
- Stock and toolpaths react as they do to a manual rotate today (stock re-fits if it is fitted to the model; operations go stale).

## Done means
Face -> G17/G18/G19 and two edges -> G17/G18/G19 both orient the model exactly (normal within a tight angular tolerance of the target axis; edge along the target axis), undo restores the previous orientation, the refusals fire by name, pinned by app tests (rotation math on known faces/edges of a fixture block and a tilted fixture) and a UI test of the pick flow.

Related: #326 (per-setup part alignment), #316 (transform between setups), #187 (3-2-1 work offset align), #315, #196 / PR #328, #308.

title: Align the part to a setup's frame (stock follows), separate from the G54 work offset

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Part of the multi-setup chain (#308). No issue in the chain lets the user **orient the part for a setup** so its stock comes out correctly oriented. Today there are only two levers, and both are wrong for this:

- **`MoveModel`** (`crates/app/src/commands/move_model.rs`) places the part rigidly in the *document* - one pose for every setup. Re-orienting it for setup 2 re-orients it for setup 1 too.
- **3-2-1 / "Set WCS orientation from selection"** (#187) rotates the *work offset* (G54...), not the part. Posting a rotated offset is now refused by name (#315, PR #325), so it can't orient a part for machining either.

The stock is an axis-aligned grid in world (`stock_sim.rs`: "The document's stock, as an axis-aligned grid in world"), so a part whose faces aren't square to world gets a stock box that doesn't match how it sits on the machine.

## Two different frames - keep them apart
1. **Setup frame (the setup's "global" / machine-table frame):** how the part sits on the machine for this setup - which face is up, which edge runs along X. The part is placed into this frame by a per-setup rigid transform. **The stock is built axis-aligned in this frame** (box/cylinder/from-model all follow), and toolpaths are generated in it. This is where a 3-2-1 / face-edge-bore pick belongs: "this face is the table, this edge is +X".
2. **Work offset (G54..G59, #196):** where program zero sits on the already-aligned part - normally a pure translation (corner, centre, top of stock, a bore). Rotation on the offset stays the exception (probing compensation), refused for now (#315).

## Proposal
- **Per-setup part alignment:** an undoable `AlignPartToSetup` command (or the `SetSetupTransform` of #316 - one stored transform part -> setup frame, not two) driven by:
  - 3-2-1 picks (primary face -> setup -Z/table, secondary edge/face -> +X, tertiary -> +Y), reusing #187's pick machinery but writing the **part's** transform, not the offset's;
  - presets (face up / flip about X/Y / rotate 90/180/270 about Z);
  - numeric entry.
- **Stock follows:** stock bounds/fit (incl. Fit to Models, #230) are computed in the setup frame from the transformed part; the viewport shows the setup with the part aligned and the stock square to it.
- **Work offset after alignment:** the G54 picker/placement (#196) works on the aligned part (corner/centre/top presets), translation only by default.
- **Posting/verification:** toolpaths, sim and the verifier all run in the setup frame; the posted coordinates are setup-frame minus the offset translation. No rotated offset needed for an aligned part, so #315's refusal no longer bites in normal use.
- Existing documents: identity transform per setup = exactly today's behaviour (implicit-setup law); saved files without the key load identically.

## Relation to the chain
- Shares storage with **#316** (the part -> setup transform *is* this alignment; the transform between two setups is derived from their two alignments). Do this with or before #316; #317-#319 consume it.
- Needs **#196** (offset per setup) for the work-offset half; complements **#315** (refuse rotated offsets) and **#187** (picks).
- Lathe: the fitted spindle axis already defines the turning frame (lathe axis-fit work); this issue is milling/mill-turn setups first.

## Done means
A part can be aligned to a setup by 3-2-1 picks, presets or numbers through an undoable command; the stock (box, cylinder, from model, Fit to Models) is axis-aligned in that setup's frame; generation, sim, verify and post run in the setup frame and post correct coordinates with an unrotated G54 placed on the aligned part; two setups can hold the same part in different orientations without touching each other; identity alignment posts byte-identically to today; pinned by tests for each.

title: Program sim: carry the machined body into the next setup through the setup transform

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Part of #308. Depends on #316 (setup transform).

## Research outcome (public literature)
Re-sampling a volumetric workpiece onto a new axis-aligned grid after a flip or 90 deg turn loses accuracy at the grid pitch, for single dexel and tri-dexel alike - tri-dexel reduces directional bias but is not rotation-invariant (Stifter 1995, dexel critique; Inui et al., triple-dexel; Museth 2013 / OpenVDB keep the sparse grid separate from its transform). The recommended design is one **canonical workpiece in the part frame**, evaluated through each setup's transform, re-sampled only where an axis-aligned grid is unavoidable. Exact B-rep booleans (#27 Solidcore) avoid resampling at a higher cost; the field/SDF engine and dual contouring (#23, PR #280) already exist.

## Today
`stock_sim::simulate_document` -> `clip_to_setup_stock` only lowers dexel columns to the next block's top - it never moves what the previous setup cut; a rotated or from-model stock in a later setup refuses the sim outright.

## Proposal
- Carry setup N's machined body into setup N+1 through the transform: the field engine in the part frame, sampled through the transform; the dexel engine re-samples on entry where it must, with the pitch stated in the verdict.
- Where it cannot judge (no transform, unsupported stock kind) keep the conservative CLIP or the named refusal - never a guessed body.

## Done means
A two-setup part (face + pocket on top, flip, pocket underneath) simulates with the underside pocket cut into what setup 1 left; the verdict matches a single-setup reference within a stated tolerance; refusals stay named.

title: Setups: a stored rigid transform between setups (flip / rotate presets, from the work offset or a datum)

body:

## Need
Carrying stock from one setup into the next needs the rigid transform between the setups' part placements. `SetupDef { stock, wcs, datum_from }` (`crates/app/src/commands/setup.rs`) has none: M3.2 A deferred it ("the transform is M3.3 ... rotation/flip matrices deliberately do not exist yet") and M3.3 shipped posts instead.

## Proposal
- Store on each setup a rigid transform part -> setup frame (rotation + translation, finite-checked), defined from: the setup's work offset placement and orientation (#196, #187); presets for the common re-clamps (flip about X, flip about Y, rotate 90/180/270 about Z); or a datum transfer from another setup (`datum_from`).
- An undoable `SetSetupTransform` command, saved and loaded; rigid only, rotation orthonormal by construction; a non-rigid or non-finite transform is refused by name at command creation.

## Done means
Each setup's transform round-trips through save/load and undo/redo; presets give the expected matrices (pinned); a document with no transform behaves exactly as today (implicit-setup law).

title: A rotated work offset posts unrotated coordinates (WCS rotation from 3-2-1 / SetWcsOrigin is dropped)

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Safety or crash: wrong output, gouge, data loss

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Part of #308. Found while researching it (code reading on `main` 2026-11-08; **not yet reproduced by a test - the first step is a pinning test**).

## What happens
A work offset can carry a rotation: `SetWcsOrigin` stores `rot`, and the 3-2-1 alignment (#187, PR #201) sets roll/pitch/yaw from a picked face and edge. Posting passes only the offset's **translation**:
- `posting::wcs_context` returns `(slot, origin)` with `origin = [pos.x, pos.y, pos.z]` - the rotation is dropped;
- the post engine emits only `OriginX/Y/Z` (`crates/post/src/post/mod.rs`), and the shipped posts (e.g. `fanuc.cps` `wo()`) subtract that origin from world coordinates.

So a toolpath for a part aligned with a rotated work offset posts world-axis coordinates shifted by the origin, not rotated into the offset's frame - on the machine, a toolpath turned against the part, with no diagnostic. No test posts with a non-identity offset rotation (every posting/setups test uses `IDENTITY_Q`).

## Fix
1. Pinning test: place G54 with a 90 deg yaw (or via `align_321` on a turned block), generate a contour, post; assert what the program says.
2. Minimum safe fix (Prime Directive): the post gate - and generation's law checks, which read `wcs_context` too - refuse by name an operation whose work offset carries a non-identity rotation, e.g. "work offset G54 is rotated (3-2-1 alignment); posting a rotated offset is not supported yet".
3. Then real support, as a user parameter with a default: the post rotates program coordinates into the offset frame, or emits the control's rotation (Fanuc G68 / G68.2, Siemens CYCLE800 / ROT, Heidenhain PLANE / CYCL 10) where the machine declares it. A G54 register is translation only on every control; rotation is either baked into the coordinates by the post or done by a control cycle. Public control documentation only.

## Done means
A rotated work offset either posts correctly rotated coordinates (pinned against a hand-computed program) or is refused by name - never a silent unrotated program.

title: MCP: no way to detect holes for a Drill, Bore or Thread operation, so they always refuse

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

body:
The MCP server (#128) can add a Drill, Bore or Thread operation, but it can't fill the operation's hole list. Those kinds machine only the holes stored in their parameters, which the app fills from its **Detect holes** button. So over MCP a drill on a model with holes always refuses.

**Reproduced on `main` 8f30bee** (`camcraft-cli mcp`): `import_model` `testdata/models/Milling-test.step`, then `set_stock` `from_model`, `add_tool` `DR-0600`, `add_operation` `{kind: "drill", source: "part"}` and `generate`. The result is "Op: nothing to machine: no holes to drill". Bore with `EM-0300-2FL` gives "boring needs at least one hole".

**Root cause (confirmed):** the hole list is filled only by the UI's `State::detect_holes` (`crates/ui/src/state.rs`). It reads `operation::holes_of` (and `cross_holes_of` on a turret machine) and commits `EditOperationParams`. The MCP tool table (`crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`) has no tool that does this, and `edit_operation` would need the agent to compute hole coordinates itself.

**Fix:** move the rule out of the UI into `operation` (one function: the op's source, recognised, written into whichever hole list the kind has, plus the radial list on a turret machine, refusing by name otherwise). The UI's button and a new MCP tool `detect_holes {name}` both call it, so an agent's holes and a click's are the same, and the edit is one undo step. Pin: an MCP test detects the holes of a plate with a through hole, generates the drill, and `undo` empties the list again.

Related: #180 (MCP picks for faces, edges and loops) is the same gap for area operations.

title: Multi-setup machining: carry the machined stock (rest body) from one setup into the next

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
## Summary

Machine a part in several setups (flip, re-clamp, rotate on a vise or fixture) where **each setup starts from the material the previous setup left** - the in-process stock ("rest body") - instead of from a fresh block. Today every setup machines, verifies and computes rest against its own declared block.

## What exists today (verified in the code)

- **Multiple setups shipped in M3.2 A** (RECOMMENDED.md "M3.2 A - Multiple setups", commit `33f5658`): `SetupDef {stock, wcs, datum_from}`, `ActiveSetup`, `CreateSetup` / `DeleteSetup` / `ActivateSetup` / `SetOperationSetup` (`crates/app/src/commands/setup.rs`), per-setup lazily spawned stock and WCS furniture (`"Setup2/Stock"`, `"Setup2/G54"`), datum transfer that clones the source's stock snap and WCS, program order rank-then-name, per-setup tool lists and setup sheets.
- **The flip transform was never built.** M3.2 A deferred it: "Placement is the flip; the transform is M3.3 ... Rotation/flip matrices deliberately do not exist yet." M3.3 shipped posts and machine definitions instead; `crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs` still says "the flip transform between setups is M3.3's engine".
- **The program sim only CLIPS between setups** (`stock_sim::simulate_document` -> `clip_to_setup_stock`): one world-frame dexel grid; entering a new setup lowers columns to at most the new block's top and never moves what the previous setup cut. A re-clamped face reads as leftover (conservative, never a gouge) - but a **rotated or from-model stock in a later setup refuses the sim outright**.
- **Rest is same-setup only**: `rest::prior_digest` / `rest::prior_state` (`crates/app/src/rest.rs`) skip operations of other setups, so a setup-2 roughing op re-cuts air where setup 1 already removed material.

## Goal

A later setup inherits the previous setup's machined stock, transformed by the re-fixturing (flip/rotation/translation), as its starting stock - for generation (rest-aware strategies skip air), for verification (gouge/rest/rapid laws judge the real material) and for display.

## Open questions (need research and decisions before breakdown)

1. **Representation of the carried body.** Dexel columns are frame-bound (Z-up grids); a flip needs re-sampling. Options: carry the field/SDF engine's volume and re-sample in the new frame; extract the machined mesh (dual contouring, #23) and re-voxelise it; or the B-rep kernel route once Solidcore lands (#27, booleans). Accuracy vs. cost vs. memory for each.
2. **Transform model.** Where does the setup-to-setup transform come from - the WCS datums (datum transfer), a picked face/edge (3-2-1 alignment, #187), a fixture definition (M3.2 B fixtures)? Is it rigid only (flip/rotate/translate) - yes for now; any tolerance on re-clamping?
3. **Interaction with existing laws.** The implicit-setup law (zero setups = legacy), the conservative CLIP law (keep as fallback?), rotated/from-model stock refusal, stamps/digests (a setup-1 regenerate must mark setup-2 ops Stale), program order.
4. **Rest across setups.** `rest::prior_*` must read the carried body; which ops consume it (adaptive, pocket, 3D rough, rest machining)?
5. **Lathe / mill-turn.** Second-op on the sub-spindle or a part flip on a lathe - same mechanism, or separate?
6. **Fixtures and collision.** The fixture solid (M3.2 B) changes per setup; collision checks must use the carried stock plus the new fixture.
7. **UI.** Showing the incoming stock per setup, choosing "start from previous setup" vs. "new block" per setup (a user parameter with a default), setup sheets.
8. **Performance.** Re-sampling a large machined body on every setup change; caching per setup.
9. **Prior art** (public documentation only, per the Clean-Room Protocol): how CAM systems describe "in-process stock" / "stock from previous setup" behaviour to users.

## Proposed breakdown (file these as sub-issues once researched)

- [ ] Research note: carried-body representation and re-sampling cost (dexel vs. field vs. mesh vs. B-rep)
- [ ] Setup-to-setup rigid transform: definition from datums / alignment, stored on the setup, undoable
- [ ] Program sim: carry the machined body into the next setup through the transform (replace or extend the CLIP law; keep refusal where it cannot judge)
- [ ] Rest across setups: `rest::prior_*` read the carried body; stamps/digests mark downstream setups Stale
- [ ] Generation: rest-aware ops in a later setup start from the carried body
- [ ] Verification: gouge / rapid / hidden-rest laws judge against the carried body
- [ ] UI: per-setup "start from previous setup" option (default on for setup 2+?), incoming-stock display
- [ ] Lathe / mill-turn second operation
- [ ] Fixture collision with carried stock

## Done means

Every sub-issue filed, linked here and closed; then this umbrella closes (AGENTS.md "needs-research is research, not code").

Related: #23 (machined mesh), #26 (dexel retirement), #27 (Solidcore), #45 (setup navigation and ordering), #187 (3-2-1 WCS alignment), #196 (WCS per setup).

title: STEP import ignores the file's length unit: a part saved in inches or metres imports 25.4x or 1000x too small
body:
The STEP importer ignores the file's declared length unit and reads every coordinate as millimetres. A part saved in metres imports 1000 times too small, and one saved in inches 25.4 times too small, with no message either way.

**Reproduced on `main` 8f30bee** (`camcraft-cli mcp`, `import_model` then `get_job`):
- `testdata/models/sample_ap214.step` declares `CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT('METRE', ...)` over `SI_UNIT(.METRE.)` (lines 73 and 349). It imports with bounds x -0.0323 .. 0.0324, y -0.0049 .. 0.0016, z -0.0324 .. 0.0858: a part about 65 x 6 x 118 mm, read as 0.065 x 0.006 x 0.118 mm.
- Boundary: `testdata/models/Milling-test.step` declares `SI_UNIT(.MILLI.,.METRE.)` and imports at its true size (x +-30, z -5 .. 20). That's correct only because millimetres is what the importer assumes.

**Root cause (confirmed):** `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step.rs::parse` passes the parsed data section to truck's `Table` and tessellates the shells. Nothing in `crates/` reads a STEP `LENGTH_UNIT` (no match for `LENGTH_UNIT`, `METRE` or `MILLI`), and there's no import scale or model scale command to correct it afterwards. `import.rs::step_real_world_file_imports` loads the metre file and checks only that the bounds are finite, so the wrong size passes.

**Why it matters:** the model is the part. A part 25.4 times too small generates, verifies and posts a correct-looking program at the wrong size, the silent wrong answer the Prime Directive rules out. Inch STEP exports are common, and three of the shipped machines are inch Tormachs.

**A fix:** read the `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT`'s `LENGTH_UNIT`. That's either an `SI_UNIT` with an optional prefix (`.MILLI.`, `.CENTI.`, none), or a `CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT` (`'INCH'`, `'FOOT'`, `'METRE'`) whose `LENGTH_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` gives the factor. Scale the tessellated vertices to millimetres. A file whose unit can't be read should import with a visible note, or be refused by name, never silently assumed. Pin: `sample_ap214.step` imports about 65 mm wide, `Milling-test.step` is unchanged, and a small inch STEP fixture imports 25.4 times its numbers.

Related, not this bug: STL and OBJ carry no unit at all, so an inch STL also imports small. An import-units choice for unitless formats is a separate decision.

Suggested labels (I can't set them): `bug`, `P1`, `area:build` or the import area, `source:agent`.

title: Deburr links its edge runs with a diagonal rapid straight from cutting depth through the part
body:
Deburr leaves every edge run except the last with one diagonal rapid, straight from cutting depth to the next run's start at the clearance plane. The cone is still engaged in the edge it just broke when it rapids up and across the part.

### Measured (main 8f30bee)

The brick from `operations.rs`'s deburr test (`cube((-20,-10,0), (20,10,10))`), stock = the brick, `CM-0600-90`, width 2, window z 6..8. The first moves:

`
move 1: Plunge (-20,-10,25) -> (-20,-10, 8)
move 2: Feed   (-20,-10, 8) -> ( 20,-10, 8)    breaks the front rim
move 3: Rapid  ( 20,-10, 8) -> (-20, 10,25)    <- from cutting depth, diagonally across the part
move 4: Plunge (-20, 10,25) -> (-20, 10, 6)
`

- Generator verify: `RapidInStock` at moves 3, 8 and 13, one per link, so the post is blocked.
- Program sim: the deepest gouge columns (worst 3.80 mm at the (20, -10) corner) sit along those links, deeper than the 2 mm break itself. (The break being charged as a gouge at all is #303.)

### Cause

`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/deburr.rs`, the run loop (lines 235-247): each run opens with `Rapid` to `(first.x, first.y, clearance_z)` from wherever the previous run ended. The vertical retract to clearance is only pushed once, after the last run (lines 248-253).

### Fix

Leave each run straight up to the clearance plane before the traverse, the same move the path already ends with. Pin: every rapid that starts below the clearance plane is vertical, and the brick's deburr verifies with no `RapidInStock`.

**Root cause (confirmed):** `finishing3d/deburr.rs`'s run loop pushes the traverse rapid without a retract first. Measured on the brick: move 3 is `Rapid (20,-10,8) -> (-20,10,25)`, and verify flags `RapidInStock` at 3, 8 and 13.

title: Post gate refuses every 2D Chamfer and Deburr: the program sim judges the intended edge break as a gouge
body:
A 2D Chamfer or a Deburr generates with no warnings, but the post gate refuses it as a gouge. The program sim judges the edge break the operation exists to cut against the model's sharp edge. So no chamfer or deburr program can post whenever the sim judges it, which is any milled program in a box or model stock.

### Measured (main 8f30bee, scratch app test, the commands only)

Part: the 40 x 20 x 10 brick from `operations.rs`'s deburr test (`cube((-20,-10,0), (20,10,10))`). Stock: `FromModel` of the brick, a finished part, so nothing else is cut. Tool: `CM-0600-90`.

| Operation | Generator verify | Post gate |
|---|---|---|
| 2D Chamfer, kind defaults (width 0.8, 45 deg, side auto, top of model) | **0 warnings** | `gouge: program cuts below the model in 624 cell(s), worst 0.74 mm at (19.94, -9.81, z 9.26)` |
| Deburr, the suite's own params (width 2, window z 6..8) | 3 `RapidInStock` (a separate bug, filed separately) | `gouge: ... 1544 cell(s), worst 3.80 mm` |

For the Deburr I binned the gouge columns by depth: **1455 of the 1544 are 2 mm deep or less**. That's the 2 mm chamfer band itself; the 89 deeper ones are where its link rapid drags the cone. So even with clean links the deburr can't post.

### Why

- `stock_sim::simulate_document` judges the simulated stock against "the part as the machine must leave it": every model's facets, minus stock and fixtures (`stock_sim.rs`). `deviate_field` then charges every column cut more than `DEV_TOL` (0.01 mm) below the model as a gouge.
- The model has a sharp edge, and the chamfer and deburr ops cut a bevel into it by design. `operation/generate.rs` already says so for the leave-stock rule ("the chamfer cone owns its face outright", "the deburr cone owns its break outright"), but nothing tells the program sim.

### Possible fixes (owner's call: this is the gouge law)

1. **The ops own their break.** Before `deviate`, take each Chamfer2D or Deburr op's own swept cone (from its path and tool) away from the judged target, so their cut is "finished part" and anything else that cuts there is still judged. This keeps the gate strict everywhere else.
2. **A per-op allowance**: columns cut only by a chamfer or deburr op, within its stated width, are clean. That's simpler, but it needs per-column provenance in the sim.
3. If the intent is that a chamfer must be modelled in CAD first, the ops should refuse at generate ("the model has no chamfer here") instead of passing verify and failing at post.

A pinning test is the brick plus each op: it posts, and a deliberately deeper chamfer (width past the tool's reach, or a cone pushed into the wall) is still refused.

**Root cause (confirmed):** `simulate_document` judges against the model's facets only, and `deviate_field` charges every column cut more than 0.01 mm below them. Measured: 1455 of the deburr's 1544 gouge columns are 2 mm deep or less (its own break), and the 2D Chamfer gives 624 columns with a 0.74 mm worst and 0 generator warnings.

title: Post gate refuses a clean 2D Contour: the program sim reads a column 9 um inside a vertical wall as a full-height gouge
body:
A 2D Contour around the repo's own `testdata/models/Milling-test.step` generates with no warnings, but the post is refused for a 10 mm gouge that isn't there. The program sim reads a column whose centre is 9 µm inside a vertical wall as cut to the floor.

### Reproduce (main 8f30bee, `camcraft-cli mcp`, one line each)

```
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"method":"initialize","params":{}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"import_model","arguments":{"name":"part","path":"testdata/models/Milling-test.step"}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"set_stock","arguments":{"from_model":"part"}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"add_tool","arguments":{"catalog":"EM-0600-4FL"}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"add_operation","arguments":{"kind":"contour","tool":"EM-0600-4FL","source":"part","name":"Contour1","params":{"bottom_z":{"reference":"top_of_model","offset":-10}}}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"generate","arguments":{}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":6,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"verify","arguments":{}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"post","arguments":{"output":"contour.nc","post":"Fanuc"}}}
```

- `verify`: Contour1 has status ok and **0 warnings** (10 mm deep, inside the 15 mm flutes). The only finding is the gate's: `gouge: program cuts below the model in 1 cell(s), worst 10.00 mm at (22.32, 19.71, z 10.00)`.
- `post` is refused with the same line.

### What the toolpath actually does there

I checked it in a scratch app test: the same job built through the commands, every move's chords at 0.5 µm against the gouge column.

- The column's centre is (22.31802, 19.71006). The part's wall there is at y 19.71901 (the model's max Y), so the centre sits 9 µm inside the part.
- The nearest the tool centre ever comes to that point is **3.00895 mm** (move 368, a feed at z 15). With r = 3, the cutter edge stays **9 µm outside** the column centre. The path is exactly on the wall, as it should be.
- The sim (`stock_sim::simulate_document`, field arm, 0.375 mm cells) still reads that column's top at z 10, the contour's floor, so `deviate_field` reports `sim - part = 10 - 20 = -10`: a 10 mm gouge.

### Why

- `march_verdicts::deviate_field` (and the column engine's `deviate`) judge each column by height alone: the marched top at the column centre minus the part's top there. At a vertical wall, a column whose centre is a few µm inside the part flips from "full height" to "floor" on a sideways error far below the field's resolution. That error then reads as a gouge the depth of the wall.
- The viewer's eye doesn't do this. `preview::gate_tol(tol, cell)` judges a hit point by its distance to the model, with the march's landing slack (`HIT_GATE = 0.15` cells) added, and PR #288 reuses that for the machined mesh. So the post gate and the viewer can disagree about the same program.
- Whether a column centre lands in that sliver depends on the stock lattice's phase against the wall. I think that's why `lead_approach.rs`, which posts a contour on this same part in a box stock at z -7, doesn't hit it. I haven't checked that.
- A 3D Finish (BN-0600, kind defaults) on the same part with the same stock is refused with 37 gouge columns, the worst also at (22.32, 19.71) and the rest along the D's curved wall. That looks like the same mechanism, but I haven't measured those columns.

### Possible fixes (owner's call - the gouge law is the Prime Directive's)

1. Judge a gouge column against the **lowest part top within a lateral slack** of its centre (for example `gate_tol(DEV_TOL, cell)`), so a column within the field's resolution of a wall isn't charged the wall's height. It still convicts any cut that reaches past the slack.
2. Or judge the program gate the way the preview does: the distance from the marched surface point to the model, with the same gate. The gate and the viewer would then share one law.

Either way, a pinning test is this job (or a synthetic plate whose wall sits a few µm off a lattice centre), plus the existing gouge goldens to show real gouges still block.

**Also in a realistic setup** (main 8cf3c90, scratch app test): the same plate in `lead_approach.rs`'s own box stock (70 x 70 x 27 at z -7).
- A 3D Finish (`BN-0600`, kind defaults) is refused: `gouge: program cuts below the model in 37 cell(s), worst 22.01 mm at (-26.56, 13.94, z -2.01)`. Generator verify reports no gouge (only `ShankHit`).
- At that column I sampled every move at 0.01 mm. The ball reaches the column's centre line down to z -2.0103, the sim's own reading, with the line **0.00002 mm inside the ball**. The finishing ball is tangent to the wall, as it should be, and the column verdict charges the tangency as a 22 mm gouge.
- Boundary: in the same stock, a contour 10 mm deep is clean, which fits the verdict depending on where the lattice falls against the wall.

That narrows the cause. For the finish, the field reads the ball exactly, so the fault is the column verdict itself (`deviate_field` / `deviate`), not field interpolation. The contour case above (a cutter edge 9 um outside the centre, read as cut) still needs field slack on top of that.
**Root cause (confirmed):** `stock_sim::march_verdicts::deviate_field` charges a column by height alone, so a column centre 9 um inside the wall that the sim reads as cut becomes a 10 mm gouge. Measured: the cutter edge stays 9 um outside that centre, and the column reads z 10.

**Root cause (likely), not instrumented:** why the field reads that column as cut at all. My guess is the field's interpolation at 0.375 mm cells, but I didn't measure the march there.

title: cl::text drops Move::rotary (and is_prismatic ignores it)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found by the independent re-review of PR #286 (continuous C-axis, `Refs #33`).

`cl::text::to_text` (`crates/cl/src/cl/text.rs`, from #279) writes a CL dump without the new optional `Move::rotary` C angle, and `Toolpath::is_prismatic` (`crates/cl/src/cl/path.rs`) ignores it too. Nothing reaches this today: the only caller is `camcraft-motion`'s headless binary, whose face paths never carry `rotary`. But a C-live path written through `to_text` would silently lose its C word.

`TiltedFrame` (`crates/cl/src/cl/frame.rs`) also rebuilds moves with `rotary: None`, which matters only if a tilted setup is ever combined with C-live cuts.

Done means: `to_text`/`from_text` round-trip the C angle (e.g. the app golden writer's `SC` word) or refuse a path that carries one by name; `is_prismatic` returns false for a path with a stated C; `TiltedFrame` either carries `rotary` through or refuses C-live moves by name - each pinned by a test.

Part of #33.

title: Documentation site: a docs folder published with GitHub Pages (user guide + architecture)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: needs-research
labels.description: Large idea with open questions: research and file sub-issues before any code

body:
## Summary

CamCraft has no user-facing documentation. Everything a user needs (install, first run, what each operation does, how to read a refusal) is either in the README or in the owner's head, and everything a developer needs (crate map, command/undo model, testing tiers, release process) lives in `AGENTS.md`, `ROADMAP.md` and `docs/` design notes that were written for the agents building it, not for people using or extending it.

This issue proposes a documentation site: a `docs/` source tree built with **mdBook** and published with **GitHub Pages**, containing

1. a **user guide** (install, UI tour, setups/stock/WCS, tools, operations, simulation and verification, posts and machines, the MCP server, troubleshooting and refusals, FAQ);
2. an **architecture / developer guide** (crate map, ECS and commands/undo, layering rules, testing tiers and gate, release process, contributing, clean-room protocol);
3. a link to the **API reference** (`cargo doc` output built in the same pipeline and placed under `/api/`).

Research is not finished: the open questions below (versioning, custom domain, repo visibility, and what counts as "in sync" with releases) need decisions before this can be broken into implementation issues. Nothing here is to be built until those are answered.

## Goals

- A new user can install, open a model and post a verified program from the guide alone.
- A new developer can find the crate that owns a behaviour, the command that changes it, and the gate that proves it, in under five minutes.
- Refusals are explained: each refusal the app can emit by name has an entry saying what it means and what to change.
- The site builds cheaply, deploys only on purpose, and cannot silently drift from the code (link check, PR checklist).
- Internal notes in `docs/` keep working for agents and for `docs/decisions/` and are not published.

Non-goals: translating the site; replacing `AGENTS.md` (which stays the agent contract); publishing `ROADMAP.md`, `RECOMMENDED.md` or the decision ledger; hosting the binaries (they stay on GitHub Releases).

## Current state (verified in the repo)

- `docs/` holds four internal notes only: `CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`, `M4.1-CRATE-SPLIT.md`, `M5-PHASE5-PLAN.md`, `spike-egui-go-no-go.md`. There is no `docs/decisions/` folder on `main` yet, although `AGENTS.md` and the agent workflow refer to one (issue branches write `docs/decisions/<N>-<slug>.md`).
- `README.md` has the product description, a download section, build instructions, testing, workspace layout, project documents and issue reporting. It is the only user-facing text.
- Crates (`crates/`): `app`, `cl`, `geometry`, `kernel`, `motion`, `post`, `sim`, `tools`, `ui`. Each crate's one-line purpose needs confirming from its `lib.rs` header when the architecture guide is written; `AGENTS.md` names `geometry`, `cl`, `tools`, `post`, `sim`, `motion` as the M4.1 split.
- `assets/`: `ui/` (Tabler-derived toolbar/tree PNGs, `LICENSES.md`, `fonts/`), `posts/` (`.cps` post scripts, plus an `AGENTS.md` inside), `machines/` (`.mch` machine files, plus an `AGENTS.md`), `themes/`, `scripts/`.
- `crates/ui/tests/snapshots/` holds egui snapshot goldens, so the UI can already be rendered headlessly for screenshots.
- `CHANGELOG.md` (one row per behaviour change, `commit | date | change | version`) and `RELEASE_NOTES.md` exist; release notes per cut are written by the release process.
- `scripts/` has `gate.ps1` (gate tiers), `release.ps1`, `sign.ps1`, `installer.ps1`, and packaging scripts for Linux (AppImage, Flatpak, Snap), macOS, and a `README.md`.
- Workflows: `ci.yml` (manual `workflow_dispatch`), `nightly.yml` (manual/nightly), `release.yml` (tags `vX.Y.0` plus `workflow_dispatch`), `aur-package.yml`. No Pages workflow exists.
- Actions budget (`AGENTS.md`): 3000 minutes per month, Windows 2x, macOS 10x, and no `push`, `pull_request` or `schedule` triggers without the owner's say-so.
- Repo is `NeoTech/Camcraft`. Whether it is public (Pages on a private repo needs a paid plan) is not verified here; see open questions.

## Options compared

| Option | Pros | Cons | Actions cost | Fit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **mdBook** | Rust-native and the rust-lang standard (`rust-lang/book`, `rustc-dev-guide` use it). Built-in search. Single binary, Markdown plus `SUMMARY.md`, fast builds. Preprocessors for mermaid (`mdbook-mermaid`) and link checking (`mdbook-linkcheck`, and the `mdbook-linkcheck2` fork that rustc-dev-guide uses). | No versioning; no first-class multi-version site. Mermaid and link check are third-party preprocessors to pin. Less theming than Docusaurus. | ~1-3 billed minutes per run on `ubuntu-latest` (1x), dominated by installing the prebuilt binary; a `cargo install` would add many minutes, so do not compile it in CI. | **Best** for a book-shaped guide written by and for Rust developers. |
| **Zola** | Single binary, fast, Rust-based. | Search needs wiring (index generation plus a front-end). Mermaid via shortcode or JS. No versioning. Smaller ecosystem for docs. | Similar to mdBook (~1-3 min). | Workable, but more glue than mdBook for the same result. |
| **MkDocs Material** | Polished default theme; strong built-in search; `pymdownx.superfences` gives mermaid; `mike` provides per-version docs. | Python toolchain in CI (pip install, slower and more cache work); a second language ecosystem beside Rust. | ~2-4 min (pip install dominates unless cached). | Strong alternative if versioned docs are a must; costs a Python toolchain. |
| **Docusaurus** | Versioned docs are first-class (`docs:version`); MDX; good theming. | Node/npm toolchain and heavier builds (typically several minutes per run); search needs a plugin or Algolia; overkill for a single-product guide. | ~4-8 min per run (npm install and build). | Best versioning, but the heaviest to run and maintain. |

Notes on the table: Perplexity's sources directly substantiate mdBook's built-in search, its use by rust-lang, and `rustc-dev-guide`'s use of mdbook-linkcheck2 and mdbook-mermaid. Feature details for Zola, MkDocs Material and Docusaurus are from general knowledge and must be checked against their official docs before any of them is chosen. Current versions observed: `mdbook-linkcheck` v0.7.7, `mdbook-mermaid` v0.17.1 (both from release listings, not verified for compatibility with the mdBook version we would pin).

Publishing source, both are viable with the same generator:

- **Actions artifact + `actions/upload-pages-artifact` + `actions/deploy-pages`**: the site is built in CI and never committed. Recommended. Pages is then configured to "GitHub Actions" as source.
- **Branch + folder (`/docs` on a `gh-pages` branch)**: requires committing generated HTML, which conflicts with "generated output is never committed" (the graphify rule applies the same way). Rejected.

## Recommendation

**mdBook**, published by an Actions workflow that uploads the built book as a Pages artifact.

Reasons:

1. It is the Rust-standard tool for this shape of document; contributors who know Rust know its layout.
2. Built-in search with no extra setup, which is the thing users ask for first.
3. Its CI is one binary download plus a build, which is the cheapest of the four on the Actions budget.
4. The source is plain Markdown in the repo, reviewable in the same PR flow as code (see the PR checklist below).
5. Versioning is the one real gap. For a pre-1.0 app that cuts minor releases, "latest plus the last release tag" is enough at first; a versioned tree is a follow-up decision (open questions).

Revisit only if the versioned-docs requirement becomes hard before 1.0; then MkDocs Material + `mike` is the fallback.

## Proposed folder layout

Keep the existing internal notes and the book source apart so mdBook only reads what is meant to be published:

```
docs/
  CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md            internal design notes (unchanged, not published)
  M4.1-CRATE-SPLIT.md            internal
  M5-PHASE5-PLAN.md              internal
  spike-egui-go-no-go.md         internal
  decisions/                     internal decision records (not published)
  guide/                         NEW - the published site (mdBook project root)
    book.toml                    mdBook config (src = "src", mermaid + linkcheck preprocessors)
    src/
      SUMMARY.md                 the table of contents; the only index of the book
      intro.md
      user/                      user guide
        install.md
        first-run.md
        ui-tour.md               panes, ribbon, browser, properties
        setups-stock-wcs.md
        tools-library.md
        operations/              one page per operation family
          2d.md  3d.md  drilling.md  turning.md  multiaxis.md  probe.md
        heights-linking.md
        simulation.md            rest material, gouge, deviation
        posts-machines.md        .mch and .cps
        mcp-server.md            MCP server for AI agents
        troubleshooting.md       refusals, read by name
        faq.md
      dev/                       architecture / developer guide
        architecture.md          crate map and layering rules
        ecs-commands-undo.md
        testing-gates.md         tiers (quick/batch/release), where tests live
        release.md               the cut process as a reader sees it
        contributing.md          claim-by-comment, draft PRs, clean-room
        clean-room.md
      api.md                     pointer to the cargo doc output at /api/
    images/                      our own renders only (see Assets policy)
  guide/book/                    BUILD OUTPUT - gitignored, never committed
```

- Internal notes stay in `docs/` root and `docs/decisions/` and are not referenced from the book. The book does not link to internal notes; where a user-facing fact lives only in a note, the fact is moved into the book.
- `docs/guide/book/` is ignored by git (`.gitignore`), and the Pages artifact is built from it, not committed.
- `README.md` stays the product front page; it links to the site once it exists. The site does not replace it.
- API reference: `cargo doc --no-deps` for the workspace crates, copied to `site/api/` by the workflow. Crates not marked `publish = false` need confirming; this is about links to rustdoc, not crates.io.

File naming: lowercase, hyphenated, one topic per file; `SUMMARY.md` is the only index. Each operation family page is named by the family (`2d.md`), not by vendor or HSMWorks name.

Ownership: the owner (NeoTech) approves structure and voice; each feature PR that changes user-visible behaviour updates the matching page (see Maintenance). Agents draft pages in their issue branch like any other change.

## Publishing pipeline

- **Trigger:** `workflow_dispatch` (manual) and tag push on minor/major tags only, matching `release.yml`'s `vX.Y.0` rule, so a docs build happens at each cut and on demand. No `push`, `pull_request` or `schedule` trigger (AGENTS.md Actions budget). Patch tags build nothing (release law).
- **Cost:** one `ubuntu-latest` job (1x multiplier), ~1-3 billed minutes, roughly one run per minor cut plus manual runs. Against 3000 minutes/month this is negligible; the cost is in the manual runs, so keep the job to: checkout, install prebuilt mdBook and two preprocessors (pinned versions, no `cargo install`), `mdbook build`, `cargo doc --no-deps`, link check, upload, deploy.
- **Deploy method:** `actions/configure-pages`, `actions/upload-pages-artifact`, `actions/deploy-pages`, with the `github-pages` environment. Two jobs: `build` (contents: read) and `deploy` (pages: write, id-token: write). Permissions set per job, not at top level, as in `release.yml`.
- **Branch/permissions:** Pages source set to "GitHub Actions" in repo settings (a one-time owner step); no `gh-pages` branch; no write to `main`.
- **Custom domain (optional):** configured in Settings → Pages with DNS records. With a custom Actions workflow, GitHub does not create the CNAME for you; the domain setting itself is what counts. Decide whether to add a `CNAME` file to the artifact (Perplexity's sources say it is not needed for an Actions-published site; verify before relying on it).
- **Versioning per release tag:** not decided. See open questions. Default proposal: the site always shows the latest release's docs; each cut's book is archived under `/vX.Y/` only once the versioning decision is made.
- **Link check:** `mdbook-linkcheck` on the built book (internal links and, optionally, external links with a retry budget) so a broken anchor fails the run. External link checking is noisy; default to internal links only and treat external as a warning.
- **Failure policy:** a failed docs build must not block a release tag's binary build (separate workflow, no `needs:` between them).

## Content outline

### User guide

1. **Install** - Windows installer and zip, Linux packages (TAR.GZ, DEB, RPM, AppImage, Snap, Flatpak), macOS (ZIP, DMG), AUR source package; where binaries come from (GitHub Releases); unsigned-build note (signing is secret-gated, see `release.yml`); first-launch warning text on each OS described in our own words.
2. **First run and UI tour** - opening a model (STL, OBJ, STEP); panes and the ribbon; the operation browser and the properties panel; keyboard and mouse picking; undo and redo (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y) and what they cover.
3. **Setups, stock and WCS** - creating a setup; stock shape and size; work offsets G54-G59; fixtures; machine choice (mill, 5-axis, lathe, mill-turn).
4. **Tools and tool library** - tool types, creating and editing a tool, the tool catalogue, holder and flute checks that the app enforces.
5. **Operations by family** - one page each:
   - 2D: face, contour (G41/G42 compensation), pocket, adaptive clearing, slot, trace, engrave, chamfer, circular, bore, thread milling;
   - 3D: adaptive roughing per level, waterline, parallel, scallop, radial, spiral, morph, flow, pencil, steep/shallow finishing;
   - drilling: spot, drill, peck, deep, tap, bore cycles and hole recognition;
   - turning: lathe operations and the spindle law;
   - multi-axis: 3+2 indexing, rotary contour/parallel/offset, 5-axis operations;
   - probe: whatever probe operations exist when the page is written (confirm, do not invent).
   Each page: what it is for, its parameters (named as the UI shows them), when to use it, what it refuses, a worked example with our own screenshot.
6. **Heights and linking** - clearance, retract, top, bottom heights; lead-in and lead-out; links between passes.
7. **Simulation and verification** - rest material; gouge and collision checks; deviation; what "verified" means and what it does not guarantee; the rule that unsafe output is blocked, not warned.
8. **Posts and machines** - choosing a post processor; `.cps` post scripts; `.mch` machine files; the intermediate (CLFile/`.cnc`) that posts read; dry-run advice.
9. **MCP server for AI agents** - what it exposes, how to connect an agent, what it can and cannot change (it goes through the same command history as the UI).
10. **Troubleshooting and refusals** - the refusal taxonomy: each refusal the app prints is listed by its name with the cause and the fix; how to read the diagnostic; what to send in a bug report.
11. **FAQ**.

### Architecture / developer guide

1. **Architecture overview** - the crate map from `crates/` with one-line purposes; the layering rule (ui -> app -> flecs; UI never calls `sys_*` or world-level APIs directly); where geometry, toolpaths, post and sim sit.
2. **ECS, commands and undo** - components declared in `crates/app/src/schema.rs`; the command history as single source of truth for undo/redo; ephemeral UI state is not undoable; deleting an entity frees its cached toolpath and mesh.
3. **Testing and gates** - the three tiers (quick, batch, release) from `scripts/gate.ps1`; where test binaries live; golden CLFile/G-code files under `tests/golden/`; the `crates/ui` CWD rule for snapshots.
4. **Release process** - how a minor/major cut is made (PR review, merge, release branch, tag, `release.yml` artifacts); why patch versions are not cut.
5. **Contributing** - claim-by-comment on issues; draft PRs; the `source:agent` label; labels (`P0`-`P2`, `area:*`); the commit format (conventional commits, `Fixes #N`).
6. **Clean-room protocol** - what the project does and does not use as reference (published Autodesk user docs for behaviour only; public G-code standards; handbooks; our own notes), in our own words, with the one-line provenance comment rule for modules.

## Screenshots and assets policy

- Screenshots show **our UI only**, rendered by us. Preferred source: the egui snapshot harness in `crates/ui/tests/snapshots/`, so images can be regenerated when the UI changes (a script or test that writes to `docs/guide/src/images/`).
- No HSMWorks or Autodesk screenshots, icons, text or sample output of any kind. Model and part images are generated fixtures we own.
- Icons referenced in the book come from `assets/ui/` and stay under the license recorded in `assets/ui/LICENSES.md`; the book credits nothing new.
- Images are PNG, sized for the book (no multi-megabyte screenshots); a stale-image check belongs in the follow-up issue.
- Operation-specific glyphs are drawn by us, as `AGENTS.md` requires.

## Maintenance

- **Who updates docs:** the author of a behaviour-changing PR updates the matching page in the same PR. A new operation or refusal adds its page or entry in the same PR that adds it.
- **PR checklist:** a `docs:` checklist item in the PR template (or the existing PR body) asking "does this change a user-visible behaviour, a refusal name or a crate's role? If yes, the matching `docs/guide/` page is updated." This is an AGENTS.md change and needs the owner's approval before it lands (process law).
- **Link check:** runs in the docs workflow on each cut and on demand; internal links are gating.
- **Sync with releases:** each cut's `CHANGELOG.md` row for a user-visible change has a docs entry or a `Docs:` line in the PR; the cut checklist confirms the site was built from the tag.
- **Stale-doc detection:** not automated in the first version; checked at each cut by the release process (a checklist item, not a CI job, to keep the Actions budget).

## Open questions (need decisions before breakdown)

1. **Repo visibility and Pages availability:** is `NeoTech/Camcraft` public? If private, does the owner's plan include Pages on private repos? (Affects whether this is buildable at all.)
2. **Versioning:** latest-only, or a versioned tree (`/vX.Y/`)? If versioned, how: archive copies on a `gh-pages` branch (which conflicts with the "no generated output committed" rule unless the branch is deploy-only), or build every tag in the same workflow (more minutes per run, reproducible)? Recommend deciding after the first minor cut ships.
3. **Custom domain:** wanted or not? If yes, which domain, and does the CNAME live in the artifact or only in the Pages settings?
4. **Generator confirmation:** accept mdBook? Confirm the preprocessors (`mdbook-mermaid`, `mdbook-linkcheck` vs `mdbook-linkcheck2`) and their pinned versions against the pinned mdBook version. Verify the Zola, MkDocs and Docusaurus claims in the table against their official docs before a final choice.
5. **Folder name:** `docs/guide/` (proposed) vs `book/` at the repo root vs `site/`. Decide once; the choice is in every link.
6. **Screenshot pipeline:** does the owner want the snapshot harness to write book images (a new test-side writer, so it is a `crates/ui` change), or are images hand-captured per release?
7. **Docs license:** text under the repo license, or a separate license (e.g. CC-BY) for the guide? The image and icon licenses in `assets/ui/LICENSES.md` must be respected either way.
8. **PR checklist wording:** the docs item in the PR template changes process; owner approves the wording (AGENTS.md change).
9. **Refusal catalogue source:** should the refusal list be generated from the code (a list of refusal names with a test that every name is documented) or written by hand? Generated is safer against drift and is recommended, but it needs a decision on where the list lives.
10. **Audience and tone:** one guide for both users and developers, or two sites? Proposed: one book, two parts (`user/`, `dev/`), each with its own table-of-contents heading.

## Proposed breakdown into follow-up issues

Each becomes its own issue after the open questions are answered:

- [ ] Decide open questions 1-10 and record each decision in `RECOMMENDED.md` (or `docs/decisions/`).
- [ ] Scaffold `docs/guide/` (`book.toml`, `SUMMARY.md`, empty pages) and `.gitignore` for the build output; builds locally with `mdbook build`.
- [ ] Add the docs workflow (`.github/workflows/docs.yml`, `workflow_dispatch` + minor/major tags, pinned installs, Pages artifact + deploy, link check) and the one-time owner step (Pages source = GitHub Actions).
- [ ] Write the user guide: install and first run, UI tour.
- [ ] Write the user guide: setups, stock, WCS, tools library.
- [ ] Write the user guide: operations by family (one issue per family, five families).
- [ ] Write the user guide: heights and linking, simulation and verification, posts and machines.
- [ ] Write the user guide: MCP server, troubleshooting and refusals, FAQ.
- [ ] Write the developer guide: architecture overview (crate map from each crate's header), ECS/commands/undo.
- [ ] Write the developer guide: testing and gates, release process, contributing, clean-room.
- [ ] Add `cargo doc` output to the site under `/api/`.
- [ ] Snapshot-based image pipeline for `docs/guide/src/images/` (if decided in question 6).
- [ ] PR template docs checklist item and cut checklist entry (owner approval of wording first).
- [ ] Versioned docs (only if question 2 chooses it).
- [ ] Custom domain (only if question 3 chooses it).
- [ ] Update `README.md` to link the published site.

## Done means

- `mdbook build` succeeds locally and in the docs workflow with pinned tools, with no warnings from the link check.
- The published site at the Pages URL shows: install, first run, every operation family, troubleshooting/refusals, the crate map, the testing tiers and the release process, each reachable from the table of contents.
- The docs workflow runs only on `workflow_dispatch` and minor/major tags (checked in the YAML), costs no more than the estimate on the run's Actions summary, and its trigger list is what this issue says.
- No internal design note, decision record or roadmap file is published; the artifact contains only the built `docs/guide/` tree and the `api/` output.
- Every screenshot in the book is an image of our UI, with its generator named on the page or in the build notes.
- The PR checklist and cut checklist include the docs step, approved by the owner.
- `README.md` links to the site.

## References

- mdBook guide: https://rust-lang.github.io/mdBook/
- mdBook CI guide (building and deploying): https://rust-lang.github.io/mdBook/continuous-integration.html
- mdBook repository: https://github.com/rust-lang/mdBook
- rust-lang book (built with mdBook): https://github.com/rust-lang/book
- rustc developer guide (mdBook, mdbook-linkcheck2, mdbook-mermaid): https://github.com/rust-lang/rustc-dev-guide
- GitHub Pages custom workflows: https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/using-custom-workflows-with-github-pages
- actions/deploy-pages: https://github.com/actions/deploy-pages
- GitHub Pages custom domains: https://docs.github.com/en/pages/configuring-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site/managing-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site
- mdbook-mermaid: https://github.com/badboy/mdbook-mermaid
- mdbook-linkcheck: https://github.com/Michael-F-Bryan/mdbook-linkcheck
- MkDocs Material (fallback): https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/
- Docusaurus versioning (rejected for now): https://docusaurus.io/docs/versioning
- Repo rules that constrain this: `AGENTS.md` (Clean-Room Protocol; Testing; Commits and Releases; Actions budget); `scripts/README.md` (gate tiers); `.github/workflows/release.yml` (tag trigger and permissions pattern).
